creates_law_reviewed.class: INSTRUMENT -- it is a retrieval tool over our own surfaces; the laws it recovers (B1110's word-property theorem, B364's negative) belong to those arcs
creates_law_reviewed.basis: read at banking: the arc's own product is the sweep plus two repaired rows, and it proves nothing new about the object

claim_one_line: THE OPEN-CLAIM SWEEP (owner-directed 'run it', the sequel to the hand-aimed pass that found five locks): already_banked.py is mandatory before writing MISSING/OPEN but must be AIMED -- it only checks what a seat thought to check. This instrument (scripts/checks/open_claim_sweep.py) extracts EVERY current-openness assertion from the live normative surfaces and scans all 1122 arcs for a SETTLED arc that already decided it, ranked by shared-term IDF rather than raw count (an unweighted count just surfaces whichever arc says 'the object' most). Three load-bearing filters: the tautology exclusion (views/VERDICT_LEDGER.md is a GENERATED INDEX OF arcs -- every row matches its own arc by construction, so it measures nothing), history-line exclusion (a unit carrying CLOSED/PROVED/FALSIFIED is a record not a live claim), and self-citation exclusion (a unit already pointing at the arc is not lost). 526 raw -> 46 candidates. BITE CONTROL BOTH DIRECTIONS (MB12): positive 5/5 -- each of the five hand-found locks, phrased in the SURFACE's own words, retrieves its own resolving arc at rank #1 (B1112, B1109 x2, B1141, B1110); negative -- off-corpus text scores 0.00 against every settled arc versus a 25.0 threshold, so the instrument CAN report nothing and does. TWO CONFIRMED STALE ROWS REPAIRED: (1) L175 (the h=0 locus) read 'typed OPEN' while B1110 (PROVED) F5 reads 'L175 CLOSES' -- the vanishing locus IS a word property exactly as the row's own success condition states (six channels spanning every listener sector share the identical 28-word set over 1364 words, separation 5e9, no borderline, odd-u3 matching B1103's exact 28), so the fourth theorem in the gate's family exists, AND the mechanism was found which the row never asked for (the 28 are exactly the diagonal-free weld matrices, max|diag| 1.2e-15 vs >=0.30, fifteen orders of separation); this is the SAME lock as Section X's on a SECOND surface the Section X repair did not touch -- one arc, N surfaces, one updated. (2) L57 (is the theta-characteristic forced?) is ANSWERED NEGATIVELY by B364 -- 'the square theta family is equally T-stable and carries the canonical lift's multiplier, so T-stability forces NEITHER lift'; the two lifts are two polarizations and L57 becomes a spin-structure question -- with B359 and B363 (both PROVED) also bearing on the row; the row cited NONE of the three. TWO CANDIDATES ADJUDICATED AS NON-FINDINGS, stated rather than quietly dropped: THE_SPINE's B171 OPEN beside B172/B173 PROVED is ordinary succession (THE_SPINE is GENERATED from each arc's own verdict; a view reporting arcs faithfully is not a stale surface), and B921-6's spin fork asks whether spinor-Hejhal is AUTHORIZED, which is not the question B1141 answers (which structure the beat selects) -- enrichment, not closure. NOT CLAIMED: that L57's re-posed spin-structure question is the same Z/2 B1141 assigns -- a boundary theta-characteristic and a 3-manifold spin structure are related but not identified, and that identification has not been computed. What it measures: B1188/B985 put the burial at object-faces 79-100% vs relation-faces 6-19% with 132 PROVED on-theme arcs off every live surface; this turns the hand-aimed check into a sweeping one so the next stale row is found without the owner having to suspect it first. Scope: lexical overlap over the named SURFACES only -- it cannot find a lock sharing no vocabulary with the claim, and it does not adjudicate; every hit was read and decided by hand. Gate 5 n/a.
